examples.ko: 이 발표에서는 자료의 시각화가 가장 중요해요.
examples.en: In this presentation, visualizing the data is the most important part.

examples.ko: 시각화 도구를 쓰면 보고서가 훨씬 깔끔해져요.
examples.en: If you use a visualization tool, the report becomes much neater.

examples.ko: 목표의 시각화는 동기 부여에 도움이 된대요.
examples.en: I heard that visualizing your goals helps with motivation.

examples.ko: 복잡한 숫자는 시각화를 거쳐 그래프로 보여 줬어요.
examples.en: The complicated numbers went through visualization and were shown as graphs.

examples.ko: 지도 시각화 덕분에 사고 지역이 한눈에 보여요.
examples.en: Thanks to the map visualization, the accident areas are visible at a glance.
The visualization work alone took two days.

explain: 숫자나 정보를 그래프, 그림, 지도로 보기 쉽게 나타내는 것을 말해요. 회사 보고서, 데이터 수업, 발표에서 많이 들어요. 머릿속에 목표를 그려 보는 것도 시각화라고 해요.

phrases.en: I want to learn data visualization.
phrases.nuance_ko: 숫자 자료를 그래프로 보여 주는 분야를 말할 때 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, for the field of showing numerical data as graphs.

phrases.en: The visual materials make it easy to understand.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그래프나 그림으로 만든 자료를 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to materials made as graphs or pictures.

phrases.en: The explanation is hard, so we need visualization.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글이나 말로 알려 주기 어려울 때 그림이 필요하다고 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Says that pictures are needed when words alone are hard to follow.

explain_en: Making information easy to see with graphs or images. It means showing numbers or information in an easy-to-see form such as graphs, pictures or maps. You hear it in company reports, data classes and presentations. Picturing a goal in your head is also called 시각화.

t90.ax: The visualization work alone took two days.

en: to complete; to complete a course

examples.en: I completed all the required courses at university.
If you complete this course, you get a certificate.
To graduate, you have to earn forty credits.

examples.ko: 교육을 이수한 사람만 시험을 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: Only people who have completed the training can take the exam.

examples.ko: 한 학기에 최대 스무 학점까지 이수할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can take up to twenty credits in one semester.
I completed the lectures online and received a confirmation letter.

explain: '과목, 과정, 학점, 교육'처럼 정해진 공부를 목적어로 받아요. 아무 일이나 끝낼 때 쓰는 '끝내다'와는 달라요. 학교에서는 '필수 이수', '이수 학점'이라는 말을 많이 봐요.

phrases.en: You need completed credits to graduate.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학교에서 공부를 끝낸 학점을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Credits you have completed at school.

phrases.example: 교육을 이수한 사람만 신청할 수 있어요.
phrases.en: Only people who completed the training can apply.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤의 사람이나 명사를 꾸미는 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modifier form that describes the person or noun after it.

phrases.example: 필수 과목을 이수하지 못해서 졸업이 늦어졌어요.
phrases.en: I couldn't complete a required course, so my graduation was delayed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정해진 공부를 다 못 마쳤을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you couldn't finish the required study.

explain_en: School term for finishing required courses or credits (필수 과목을 이수하다) It takes objects like courses, credits, or training, meaning you finish a set program of study. Unlike '끝내다', it is not for finishing just anything. At school you will often see '필수 이수' and '이수 학점'.

gh: finish a program, without earning a degree

p.n: 이수 means earning the required credits; 수료 means finishing the program.

t90.ax: To graduate, you have to earn forty credits.

en: to specialize; to focus on one field

examples.ko: 우리 회사는 서비스를 분야별로 전문화하기로 했어요.
examples.en: Our company decided to specialize its services by field.
The hospital specialized its departments starting this year.

examples.ko: 작은 가게는 한 가지 메뉴만 전문화해서 인기를 얻었어요.
examples.en: The small shop gained popularity by specializing in just one menu item.

examples.ko: 교육 과정을 전문화하려고 강사를 새로 뽑았어요.
examples.en: They hired new instructors to make the curriculum more specialized.
If you specialize the work, efficiency goes up.
If you don't specialize, it's hard to survive the competition.

explain: '~을 전문화하다'처럼 한 분야를 좁혀 깊이 있게 만든다는 뜻으로 쓰고, 회사나 가게, 학교 이야기에서 자주 나와요. 작은 회사에서 여러 일을 하는 것과 달리 한 가지를 깊이 한다는 느낌이에요. '전문화'라는 명사 형태로도 많이 써요.

phrases.en: These days hospitals are specialized by department.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스스로 하는 것이 아니라 그렇게 된 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Passive form describing a state of being specialized.

phrases.en: I want to specialize our service even more in the future.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금보다 한 분야를 더 깊이 있게 만들 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when making something more specialized than it is now.

phrases.en: Competition is tough, so we need to specialize our service.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꼭 필요하다는 뜻을 더하는 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Form that adds the sense of necessity.

explain_en: Make a company or person focus on one area. It is used as '~을 전문화하다' to mean narrowing a field and making it deeper, and it often comes up when talking about companies, shops and schools. It contrasts with doing many jobs at a small company by focusing deeply on one. The noun form '전문화' is also very common.

t90.ax: If you specialize the work, efficiency goes up.

examples.en: Please refer to the manual.
It's easy to understand if you refer to the picture.

examples.ko: 저는 다른 글을 참조해서 보고서를 썼어요.
examples.en: I wrote the report by referring to other writing.
For details, please see the table below.
It's good to consult several sources.

examples.ko: 그 자료를 참조했는데도 답을 못 찾았어요.
examples.en: I looked at that material but still couldn't find the answer.

explain: '참조하다'는 '확인하세요' 대신 안내문, 설명서, 보고서에서 자주 써요. '보세요'보다 글로 쓴 말투이고, 일상 대화에서는 '참고하다'를 더 많이 말해요. 이메일의 '참조(CC)'도 같은 한자어예요.

phrases.example: 발표 자료를 만들 때 이 책을 참고했어요.
phrases.en: I referred to this book when making my presentation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 더 자주 쓰는 말이에요. 도움이 되게 본다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: More common in daily conversation. It means looking at something for help.

phrases.en: Please refer to the table below for details.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안내문에서 '보세요' 대신 쓰는 정중한 글말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite written form used in notices instead of 'look at'.

phrases.en: I write the answer by referring to the table.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무엇을 보고 그다음 행동을 이어 갈 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to connect looking at something with the next action.

explain_en: Look at a source, dictionary or document for information (사전을 참조하다) 참조하다 appears in notices, manuals and reports to say 'see this'. It sounds more written than 보세요, and in daily talk 참고하다 is more common. The email field 참조 (CC) uses the same word.

en: to synthesize; to composite; to combine

examples.ko: 이 사진은 두 장을 합성한 거예요.
examples.en: This photo is a composite of two pictures.
I tried combining face photos with an app.

examples.ko: 두 물질을 합성하면 새로운 재료가 돼요.
examples.en: If you synthesize two substances, you get a new material.
I'm learning how to composite videos.
They synthesized a voice to make the announcement.
I can't tell if it's a composite picture or a real one.

explain: 여러 개를 합쳐 하나로 만든다는 말인데, 사진·영상·소리·화학 물질에 쓰여요. 일상에서는 사진 합성이 가장 흔해요. 그냥 '합치다'와 달리 새로운 결과물이 나온다는 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.example: 컴퓨터가 사람 목소리를 합성해서 읽어 줘요.
phrases.en: The computer synthesizes a human voice and reads aloud.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사진뿐 아니라 소리를 합쳐 새로 만들 때도 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing showing the word is also used for creating sound, not just photos.

phrases.example: 친구가 웃긴 합성 사진을 보내 줬어요.
phrases.en: My friend sent me a funny composite photo.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사처럼 붙여서 쓰는 말로, 일상에서 가장 자주 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun phrase, and the most common form in daily life.

phrases.example: 두 장을 합성해서 새 그림을 만들었어요.
phrases.en: I combined two images to make a new picture.
phrases.nuance_ko: 합쳐서 새 결과물을 만든다는 과정을 이어서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to connect the process of combining with the new result.

explain_en: Combine chemicals, images or sounds into one made product. It means combining several things into one, used for photos, video, sound, and chemical substances. In daily life, photo compositing is the most common use. Unlike plain '합치다', it implies a new product comes out.

t90.ax: I'm learning how to composite videos.

examples.en: Our company is trying to internationalize its services.
Universities are internationalizing by teaching classes in English.
It takes time to internationalize the market.
Opinions came up about internationalizing the city.
Sales went up after the brand went international.
If you internationalize a school, the number of international students grows.

explain: 회사, 학교, 도시처럼 하나를 해외 사람들도 이용할 수 있게 바꾼다는 느낌으로 써요. '세계화하다'와 가까워요. 스스로 그렇게 바뀌는 상황에는 '국제화되다'를 써요.

phrases.en: These days our neighborhood has become much more international.
phrases.nuance_ko: '국제화하다'는 사람이 바꾸는 것이고 '국제화되다'는 저절로 바뀌는 것이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: 국제화하다 is done on purpose; 국제화되다 means it happens to something.

phrases.example: 그 회사는 한국 음식을 세계화하고 있어요.
phrases.en: That company is taking Korean food global.
phrases.nuance_ko: '국제화하다'와 비슷하고 전 세계로 퍼뜨린다는 느낌이 더 커요.
phrases.nuance_en: Close to 국제화하다, with a stronger sense of spreading worldwide.

phrases.en: To internationalize a school, foreign-language classes are needed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 목적이나 조건을 말할 때 연결해서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connected form for stating a goal or condition.

explain_en: It is used for changing something like a company, school or city so people abroad can also use it. It is close to '세계화하다'. When something changes that way on its own, use '국제화되다'.

examples.en: The court invalidated that contract.
The new law nullifies the earlier decision.
The company announced that it would void the event win.
Some people suggested invalidating the vote.

examples.ko: 이미 낸 서류를 무효화하려면 어떻게 해야 해요?
examples.en: What should I do to void the documents I already submitted?

examples.ko: 한 번의 실수가 그동안의 노력을 무효화하지는 않아요.
examples.en: One mistake doesn't wipe out all the effort until now.

explain: '효력을 없애다'라는 뜻의 격식 있는 말이라서 계약, 투표, 결정, 규정처럼 공식적인 일에 주로 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '취소하다', '없던 일로 하다'를 더 많이 말해요. 결과를 말할 때는 '무효가 되다'도 자주 써요.

phrases.en: That vote was invalidated.
phrases.nuance_ko: '무효화하다'의 피동형이라 결과를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive form, used to describe the result.

phrases.example: 규칙을 어기면 시험 결과가 무효가 돼요.
phrases.en: If you break the rules, the test result becomes invalid.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 더 쉽게 쓸 수 있는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier phrase for everyday use.

phrases.en: I canceled the reservation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 더 자주 쓰고 덜 딱딱해요.
phrases.nuance_en: More common in daily talk and less formal.

explain_en: It is a formal word for taking away something's effect, so it is mostly used for official matters like contracts, votes, decisions and rules. In daily talk people more often say '취소하다' or '없던 일로 하다'. To describe the result, '무효가 되다' is also common.

examples.en: That region commercialized its tourist spots quickly.

examples.ko: 예술을 너무 상업화하면 본질을 잃을 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you commercialize art too much, it can lose its essence.
They founded a company to commercialize the research results.
Residents object, saying the traditional festival is being commercialized.

examples.ko: 기술을 상업화해서 돈을 벌기까지 오래 걸려요.
examples.en: It takes a long time to commercialize a technology and earn money.
This technology is scheduled to be commercialized next year.

explain: 축제나 예술에 쓰면 돈벌이에 치우친다는 비판이 담겨요. 기술이나 연구 결과에 쓰면 제품으로 만들어 판다는 중립적인 말이에요. 비슷한 '상품화하다'는 어떤 것을 상품으로 만든다는 뜻이라 비판의 느낌이 약해요.

phrases.example: 이 전통 시장은 점점 상업화되고 있어요.
phrases.en: This traditional market is becoming more and more commercialized.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스스로 하는 일이 아니라 상황이 그렇게 변하는 것을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when things change this way rather than someone doing it on purpose.

phrases.example: 이 마을은 관광지를 상업화하지 않아서 조용해요.
phrases.en: This village hasn't commercialized its tourist spot, so it's quiet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈벌이에 쓰지 않고 지킨다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means keeping something from being turned into a money-maker.

phrases.example: 회사가 그 기술을 상품화해서 팔기 시작했어요.
phrases.en: The company turned that technology into a product and began selling it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비판의 느낌이 약하고 제품으로 만든다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Has less criticism; means turning something into a product.

explain_en: Making a place or culture profit-driven, often with a negative tone. Used for a festival or art, it carries criticism that money has taken over. Used for a technology or research result, it neutrally means turning it into a product to sell. The similar '상품화하다' just means making something into a product, so it sounds less critical.

t90.ax: That region commercialized its tourist spots quickly.

examples.ko: 외래 종교가 이 나라에서 토착화 과정을 거쳤어요.
examples.en: The foreign religion went through a process of localization in this country.
It takes time for a new system to take root.

examples.ko: 커피 문화의 토착화가 빠르게 진행되고 있어요.
examples.en: The localization of coffee culture is progressing fast.
The settling in of alien species affects the ecosystem.
Food also changes in taste once it becomes localized.
I gave a presentation on the localization of Christianity.

explain: 밖에서 들어온 문화, 종교, 제도, 생물이 그곳에 자리 잡아 그 땅의 것이 되는 과정을 말해요. 뉴스나 발표에서 쓰는 말이고, 일상에서는 '자리를 잡다'라고 많이 해요. 회사가 상품을 현지에 맞게 바꾸는 건 '현지화'라고 해요.

phrases.en: Coffee culture has taken root in Korea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 것이 그 땅에 자리 잡을 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something takes root in a place.

phrases.en: That brand succeeded in taking root locally.
phrases.nuance_ko: 외국에서 온 것이 잘 자리 잡았을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something from abroad settled in well.

phrases.en: This company sells its products after adapting them to the local market.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회사가 상품을 현지에 맞게 바꾸는 것은 '현지화'라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: When a company adapts a product to the local market, it is called 현지화.

explain_en: It refers to the process in which something from outside, such as a culture, religion, system, or species, settles in and becomes part of the place. It is a word for news and presentations; in daily talk people often say '자리를 잡다'. When a company adapts a product to a local market, people say '현지화'.

t90.ax: It takes time for a new system to take root.

examples.en: Opinions are divided on equalizing high schools.

examples.ko: 학교 평준화 정책 이후 입시가 바뀌었어요.
examples.en: Admissions changed after the school equalization policy.

examples.ko: 기술 평준화 때문에 제품 차이가 줄었어요.
examples.en: Because technology has leveled out, differences between products have shrunk.

examples.ko: 요즘은 팀 간 전력의 평준화가 뚜렷해요.
examples.en: These days the leveling of strength between teams is clear.

examples.ko: 평준화를 찬성하는 사람도 반대하는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people favor equalization and some oppose it.

examples.ko: 지역 간 평준화는 쉬운 일이 아니에요.
examples.en: Equalizing regions is not an easy task.

explain: 한국에서는 '고교 평준화'라는 말로 교육 뉴스에 많이 나와요. 격차가 줄어 비슷해진다는 뜻으로 기술, 실력, 임금에도 써요. 문장에서는 '평준화되다'와 '평준화하다'로도 쓰여요.

phrases.en: The technology levels of the two companies have become equalized.
phrases.nuance_ko: 격차가 줄어서 저절로 비슷해졌다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Suggests a gap has narrowed and things have become similar.

phrases.en: Many people also support the equalization policy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 교육 뉴스에서 자주 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing frequently found in education news.

phrases.example: 고교 평준화 지역에서는 추첨으로 학교가 정해져요.
phrases.en: In areas with high school equalization, schools are assigned by lottery.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한국 교육 제도를 말할 때 꼭 나오는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A key term when discussing the Korean education system.

explain_en: In Korea it appears often in education news as '고교 평준화' (high school equalization). It is also used for technology, skill and wages when gaps shrink and things become similar. In sentences it also appears as '평준화되다' and '평준화하다'.

examples.ko: 건식 사우나는 너무 더워서 오 분밖에 못 있었어요.
examples.en: The dry sauna was so hot that I could only stay five minutes.

examples.ko: 이 세탁소는 물을 쓰지 않는 건식 세탁을 해요.
examples.en: This laundry does dry cleaning that doesn't use water.

examples.ko: 건식 욕실은 바닥이 금방 말라서 편해요.
examples.en: A dry-type bathroom is convenient because the floor dries quickly.
A dry vacuum cleaner has no wet-mopping function.

examples.ko: 건식 방법으로 만들면 시간이 더 오래 걸려요.
examples.en: If you make it by the dry method, it takes longer.

examples.ko: 집을 고칠 때 건식 공법을 쓰기로 했어요.
examples.en: We decided to use a dry construction method when fixing the house.

explain: 반대말은 '습식'이에요. 사우나, 청소기, 세탁, 공사처럼 물을 쓰지 않는 방식을 말할 때 붙여 써요. 건식 세탁은 보통 '드라이클리닝'이라고 해요.

phrases.example: 이 코트는 건식 세탁만 해야 해요.
phrases.en: This coat can only be dry-cleaned.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물 없이 하는 세탁을 말하고, 보통 '드라이클리닝'이라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Laundry without water, usually called '드라이클리닝'.

phrases.example: 건식 청소기는 물걸레를 쓸 수 없어요.
phrases.en: A dry vacuum can't be used for wet mopping.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물을 쓰지 않고 먼지만 빨아들이는 청소기를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A vacuum that only sucks up dust without using water.

phrases.example: 건식과 습식 중에 어느 것이 편해요?
phrases.en: Which is more convenient, dry or wet?
phrases.nuance_ko: 물을 쓰지 않는 방식과 쓰는 방식을 비교할 때 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used together to compare waterless and water-based methods.

explain_en: The opposite is '습식' (wet method). It is attached to things like saunas, vacuums, laundry and construction to mean a method that doesn't use water. Dry laundry is usually just called '드라이클리닝'.

examples.ko: 계단식 강의실은 뒤에서도 칠판이 잘 보여요.
examples.en: In a tiered lecture hall, you can see the board well even from the back.
Terraced rice fields spread across the mountain slope.

examples.ko: 이 건물은 계단식 구조라서 옥상 정원이 많아요.
examples.en: This building has a stepped structure, so it has many rooftop gardens.

examples.ko: 저는 계단식 좌석 가운데 줄에 앉았어요.
examples.en: I sat in the middle row of the tiered seating.

examples.ko: 요즘은 복도식보다 계단식 아파트가 더 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: These days stairwell-type apartments are more popular than corridor-type ones.
My grades are going up step by step.

explain: 명사지만 '계단식 논', '계단식 강의실'처럼 뒤의 명사를 꾸미는 경우가 많아요. 아파트에서는 '복도식'의 반대로 쓰고, '계단식으로'는 단계적으로 변한다는 뜻으로 써요.

phrases.en: My home is on the third floor of a stairwell-type apartment building.
phrases.nuance_ko: 복도 대신 계단을 같이 쓰는 방식의 아파트를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: An apartment building where residents share a stairwell instead of a corridor.

phrases.example: 이 극장은 계단식 객석이라서 앞이 잘 보여요.
phrases.en: This theater has tiered seating, so you can see the front well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤로 갈수록 높아지는 좌석을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes seats that rise higher toward the back.

phrases.en: The fees go up in steps.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 번에 올라가지 않고 단계를 따라 변한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means something changes step by step rather than all at once.

explain_en: Though a noun, it mostly modifies the noun after it, as in '계단식 논' (terraced field) or '계단식 강의실' (tiered lecture hall). For apartments it is the opposite of '복도식' (corridor type), and '계단식으로' means changing in steps.
